title: Grep Search
description: Search for a pattern in files
code: grep "pattern" file.txt
explanation: Searches for lines containing the pattern in the file.

title: Grep Recursive
description: Search recursively in a directory
code: grep -r "pattern" /path/to/dir/
explanation: Searches all files in a directory tree for the pattern.

title: Grep Ignore Case
description: Search case-insensitively
code: grep -i "pattern" file.txt
explanation: Ignores uppercase/lowercase differences in search.

title: Grep Invert Match
description: Show lines that do NOT match the pattern
code: grep -v "pattern" file.txt
explanation: Displays lines that do not contain the pattern.

title: Grep Count Matches
description: Count number of matching lines
code: grep -c "pattern" file.txt
explanation: Returns the count of lines matching the pattern.

title: Grep Line Number
description: Show matching lines with their line numbers
code: grep -n "pattern" file.txt
explanation: Prefixes matching lines with their line numbers.

title: Grep Context Lines
description: Show lines before and after match
code:
grep -C 3 "pattern" file.txt
# Or separately:
grep -A 2 "pattern" file.txt  # After match
grep -B 2 "pattern" file.txt  # Before match
explanation: Displays context lines around matches for better understanding.

title: Grepl Extended Regex
description: Use extended regular expressions in grep
code:
grep -E "error|warning|critical" log.txt
# Or:
egrep "error|warning|critical" log.txt
explanation: Extended regex supports +, ?, {, }, |, (, ) without escaping.

title: Sed Replace First
description: Replace first occurrence of a pattern per line using sed
code: sed 's/old/new/' file.txt
explanation: Substitutes the first occurrence of 'old' with 'new' on each line.

title: Sed Replace All
description: Replace all occurrences of a pattern globally
code:
sed 's/old/new/g' file.txt
# In-place edit (modify file directly):
sed -i 's/old/new/g' file.txt
# Backup before edit:
sed -i.bak 's/old/new/g' file.txt
explanation: The 'g' flag replaces every occurrence, not just the first.

title: Sed Delete Lines
description: Delete lines matching a pattern using sed
code:
sed '/pattern/d' file.txt
# Delete specific line number:
sed '5d' file.txt
# Delete range:
sed '10,20d' file.txt
explanation: The 'd' command in sed removes lines matching the pattern or address.

title: Sed Print Lines
description: Print only matching lines with sed
code:
sed -n '/pattern/p' file.txt
# Print specific lines:
sed -n '5,10p' file.txt
explanation: The -n flag suppresses automatic printing; 'p' prints only matching lines.

title: Awk Print Column
description: Print specific columns from a file using awk
code:
awk '{print $1, $3}' file.txt
# Print last column:
awk '{print $NF}' file.txt
# With custom delimiter:
awk -F',' '{print $1}' data.csv
explanation: awk splits each line into fields ($1, $2, ...) and processes them.

title: Awk Pattern Match
description: Filter lines matching a condition using awk
code:
awk '/error/ {print}' log.txt          # Pattern match
awk '$3 > 100 {print $1, $3}' data.txt  # Numeric condition
awk 'NR > 1 {print}' file.txt           # Skip header line
explanation: awk applies patterns/conditions before executing the action block.

title: Awk Sum Average
description: Compute sum and average of a column with awk
code:
awk '{sum += $2; count++} END {print "Sum:", sum, "Avg:", sum/count}' data.txt
# With formatted output:
awk '{sum+=$3} END {printf "Total: %.2f\n", sum}' sales.csv
explanation: awk's END block runs after processing all lines, useful for aggregations.

title: Sort Lines
description: Sort lines alphabetically
code: sort file.txt
explanation: Sorts lines in alphabetical order.

title: Sort Numerically
description: Sort lines numerically
code: sort -n numbers.txt
explanation: Sorts lines based on numeric value rather than lexicographic.

title: Sort Reverse
description: Sort lines in reverse (descending) order
code: sort -r file.txt
explanation: Reverses the order of sort.

title: Sort By Column
description: Sort by a specific column/field
code:
sort -k2 file.txt           # Sort by 2nd column
sort -k2 -n file.txt        # Numerically by 2nd column
sort -t',' -k3 -n data.csv  # Sort CSV by 3rd column
explanation: The -k flag specifies which column to sort by.

title: Uniq Lines
description: Remove consecutive duplicate lines
code:
sort file.txt | uniq
# Count occurrences:
sort file.txt | uniq -c
# Show only duplicates:
sort file.txt | uniq -d
# Show only unique (non-duplicate) lines:
sort file.txt | uniq -u
explanation: uniq removes consecutive duplicates. Always sort first or only adjacent dupes are removed.

title: Cut Columns
description: Extract columns from a file
code:
cut -f1,3 file.tsv              # Extract 1st and 3rd columns (tab delimited)
cut -d',' -f2 data.csv           # Extract 2nd column of CSV
cut -c1-5 file.txt               # Extract first 5 characters per line
explanation: cut extracts columns by field (-f) with a delimiter (-d) or by character position (-c).

title: Tr Translate Characters
description: Translate, squeeze, or delete characters
code:
cat file.txt | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'   # Lowercase to uppercase
echo "hello" | tr 'a-z' 'A-Z'                 # Alternative
cat file.txt | tr -d '\r'                     # Remove carriage returns
echo "a  b   c" | tr -s ' '                  # Squeeze spaces: 'a b c'
explanation: tr replaces or deletes characters from a stream.

title: Tee Split Output
description: Write output to a file while also displaying on terminal
code:
command | tee output.txt               # Save output, show on screen
command | tee -a output.txt           # Append to file
command | tee >(grep error > errors.txt)  # Process substitution
explanation: tee reads from stdin and writes to both stdout and files simultaneously.

title: Xargs Build Commands
description: Build and execute commands from stdin
code:
find . -name "*.txt" | xargs rm           # Remove all .txt files
grep -rl "TODO" . | xargs sed -i 's/TODO/DONE/g'  # Find and replace
find . -type f | xargs -I{} cp {} /backup/         # Custom placeholder
echo '1 2 3 4' | xargs -n2                     # Run with max 2 args per command
find . -name "*.log" | xargs -P4 gzip          # Parallel (4 processes)
explanation: xargs converts stdin into command-line arguments, with options for parallel execution.

title: Diff Compare Files
description: Compare two files line by line
code:
diff file1.txt file2.txt
# Unified format:
diff -u file1.txt file2.txt
# Side-by-side:
diff -y file1.txt file2.txt
# Ignore whitespace:
diff -w file1.txt file2.txt
explanation: diff shows lines that differ between two files.

title: Diff Directory Compare
description: Compare two directories recursively
code:
diff -r dir1/ dir2/
# Show only which files differ (summary):
diff -rq dir1/ dir2/
explanation: Recursive diff compares directory structures and their files.

title: Comm Compare Lines
description: Compare two sorted files line by line
code:
comm file1.txt file2.txt              # 3 columns: lines only in 1, only in 2, common
comm -12 file1.txt file2.txt         # Show only common lines
comm -23 file1.txt file2.txt         # Show lines only in file1
comm -13 file1.txt file2.txt         # Show lines only in file2
explanation: comm shows which lines are unique to each file and which are common, but files must be sorted.

title: Watch Command
description: Run a command repeatedly and display output
code:
watch -n 5 'ls -l'                  # Run ls -l every 5 seconds
watch 'free -h'                       # Monitor memory usage
watch -d 'netstat -tulpn'             # Highlight changes
explanation: watch executes a command periodically and full-screens its output.
